name: Pad Prik Khing
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice. Cook it in a lidded saucepan with 420 ml of the measured water: bring to a boil, cover and reduce to the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes before fluffing. Meanwhile pat the tofu dry and cut it into 2 cm cubes, trim the beans into 4 cm lengths, finely slice the red chilli and lime leaves, and mince the garlic.

Check the Thai red curry paste label carefully: many brands contain animal-derived ingredients paste or animal-derived ingredients sauce. Use only a clearly vegetarian paste. Stir the paste with the soy sauce, brown sugar and remaining 80 ml measured water into a thick but pourable mixture. This is a dry stir-fry, so do not add coconut milk.

Heat 25 ml neutral oil in a wide heavy pan over medium-high heat. Lay the tofu cubes in one layer and brown for 3 minutes without moving them. Turn and cook another 3 minutes until several sides are golden; move to a plate. Use two batches if needed so the tofu does not steam.

Add the remaining 20 ml oil to the pan. Stir-fry the green beans for 4–5 minutes until bright and crisp-tender. Add the garlic and sliced red chilli for 30 seconds. Push the beans aside, add the mixed curry paste to the hot pan and fry it for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant and slightly darker.

Return the tofu and add the finely shredded lime leaves. Toss everything for 2 minutes until the red curry paste clings to the tofu and beans and the pan looks almost dry. Divide into four portions and serve with the jasmine rice alongside.
tips: Pad Prik Khing is meant to be a fairly dry red-curry-paste stir-fry rather than a coconut curry. Most non-vegetarian red curry pastes contain shrimp, so read the label every time. Lime leaves add the characteristic aroma; remove their tough centre vein before shredding.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
